meta.title: Mitday — for groups that never find a date
meta.description: For the group that has been saying “we should hang out” for months. Everyone paints the days they can make and Mitday picks the best one.

footer.tagline: Mitday · for groups that always say “we should hang out”

landing.title: No more “we should hang out”
landing.subtitle: For groups that have been trying to have dinner since last summer. Create a plan, send the link, everyone paints the days they can make and Mitday picks the best one. No 300 messages in between.
landing.ctaNote: Your friends don't need an account. Or excuses.

chat.title: Sound familiar?
chat.body: Someone suggests it, nobody commits, someone is “easy” and the plan dies at “let's play it by ear”. With Mitday the same group marks its days on one link and the best day falls out on its own, even if the easy one stays easy.
chat.m1: We need to meet up, we haven't seen each other since summer
chat.m4: Can't do this weekend. The next one?
chat.m5: Got a wedding the next one
chat.m6: What did I miss? It says 214 messages
chat.m8: Ok, let's play it by ear
chat.m9: Hey, are we meeting up or what?

past.title: People used to manage it
past.body: Documentary proof that meeting up is possible. None of these groups had a group chat, and yet.
past.p1: Picnic, 1716. Settled by letter, without a single “I'm easy”.
past.p2: Picnic at Hagidera, Japan, 18th century. Six people, one date, zero messages.
past.p3: Autumn, around 1789. Everyone came. Even the one who hears about everything last.
past.p4: Ball in Charleville, 1950. The last group to settle a date on the first try.
past.credit: Pictures: The Metropolitan Museum of Art (public domain) and State Library of Queensland (no known copyright restrictions).

types.title: Every group has one of each

adapts.title: The one who's “easy”
adapts.body: Now they prove it: “Can do”, “If needed” or “Can't”, painted day by day. Being easy about everything no longer counts.

noSignup.title: The one who signs up for nothing
noSignup.body: No need. Open the link, type a name, mark the days. Switching phones? There's a personal link.

dinner.title: The “I can only do dinner” one
dinner.body: Pick whole days, slots such as “Lunch” and “Dinner”, or an hourly grid in their own time zone.

secret.title: The one who'd rather nobody knew they can't
secret.body: You decide whether people see who can make it, only the heatmap, or nothing. Their secret is safe. You always see the full table.

late.title: The one who hears about everything last
late.body: When you close the date, they get a notice with the event for their calendar. Let's hear the excuse now.

end.title: The plan won't make itself
end.label: What the plan is for
end.note: We take you to the plan with the title already filled in. Your friends don't need an account.

demo.sample: Four example friends who, miraculously, all answered. Paint over it: tap a day or drag.
